chunks: We ask Allah, the Glorified, that He may make us and you among those whom bounty does not mislead, whom nothing can stop from obedience of his Lord, and whom regret and grief do not befall after death.
ai.seo_question: What does the supplication in Nahj al-Balagha ask for regarding the effects of bounty and death on obedience to God?
ai.summary: This supplication, characteristic of the eloquent style of Nahj al-Balagha, addresses the dual spiritual perils of abundance (which breeds arrogance) and scarcity or death (which breeds regret). It emphasizes the necessity of maintaining consistent obedience (ta'ah) to God, ensuring that worldly blessings do not lead to spiritual complacency nor worldly ends lead to posthumous remorse. The text reflects the Shia emphasis on balanced piety, where the believer remains steadfast in worship regardless of changing circumstances.
